summary: USB bus-powered 8-in/8-out 24-bit/96 kHz DJ audio interface with two switchable phono/line input pairs and DIN MIDI, built for Traktor Scratch DVS.
identityNotes: The user names it 'Traktor Audio 8 DJ'; NI sold it as 'Audio 8 DJ' (Traktor Scratch Pro bundle). No hardware revisions found. Exact connector layout (which input pairs have phono preamps) is unverified because the manual could not be opened; the manual mentions two switchable phono preamps and 8 RCA in / 8 RCA out.

tests.title: Audio 8 DJ driver installed and healthy
tests.why: No driver, unsigned driver or an error state in Device Manager is the most common reason Traktor shows no Audio 8 DJ.
steps: Connect the Audio 8 DJ directly to a USB 2.0/3.0 port on the PC (no hub).
Run the driver check.
If missing, install the Traktor Audio 8 DJ driver and reboot.

tests.why: An unsigned or legacy driver may be blocked or crash on Windows 10/11 (Secure Boot / HVCI).
steps: Run the driver check and read the signature result.

tests.title: USB port, cable and bus power
tests.why: The interface is USB bus powered; hubs, long cables or shared controllers cause dropouts and clicks.
steps: Use the supplied/short USB cable straight into the PC, not a hub or keyboard port.
Prefer a port on a different controller from other audio/USB-3 storage devices.
Flex the cable at the connector while audio plays: no dropouts.
Power LED on the unit stays steady.

tests.title: Control panel: sample rate, latency, software lock
tests.why: The control panel holds the latency/buffer setting and phono gain selectors; wrong values give clicks or low timecode level.
steps: Open the Audio 8 DJ control panel (Start menu / system tray).
Note the sample rate (44.1/48/96 kHz) and set it equal to the Traktor audio setup.
Set the latency to a value that plays 10 minutes of music without clicks.
Confirm the software-lock option is not blocking another application.

tests.title: Signal health: Input 1/2 (Deck A) LINE
tests.why: Finds a dead channel, wrong switch position, bad RCA or noisy preamp for this input pair.
steps: Set the PHONO/LINE switch for this pair to LINE.
Feed a stereo line source (phone, CD player or mixer output) at nominal level.
Run the signal health test; both channels must show signal, similar level, no clipping or dropouts.

tests.title: Signal health: Input 1/2 (Deck A) PHONO
tests.why: Finds a dead channel, wrong switch position, bad RCA or noisy preamp for this input pair.
steps: Set the PHONO/LINE switch for this pair to PHONO.
Connect a turntable with cartridge (ground wire attached) and play a 1 kHz / test record or music.
Check that the control-panel phono gain is set for your cartridge.
Run the signal health test; both channels must show signal, similar level, no clipping or dropouts.

tests.title: Signal health: output pair 1/2
tests.why: Verifies each analog output pair passes a clean stereo signal.
steps: Patch Out 1-2 RCA to a free line input of the Audio 8 DJ (loopback) or to a mixer channel and record that.
Play a 1 kHz tone/music from the DJ app to this output only.
Run the signal health test and confirm both channels equal.

tests.title: Phono channel separation (cartridge + preamp)
tests.why: Distinguishes cartridge/wiring crosstalk from preamp or input faults.
steps: Set the deck input to PHONO.
Play the left-only then right-only band of a test record.
Run the test for each deck.
equipment: Test record with L/R separation bands

tests.title: Ground and hum on phono inputs
tests.why: A floating turntable ground gives 50/60 Hz hum, only visible on phono inputs.
steps: Connect turntable ground wire to the interface ground terminal.
Lift the stylus, start the platter, run the test.
Compare with ground wire disconnected to prove it is ground related.

tests.title: Noise floor with inputs open (line)
tests.why: Establishes the idle noise of the line inputs/converters.
steps: Disconnect all cables from the line inputs, set switch to LINE.
Run signal health and read noise floor.

tests.title: Round-trip latency at chosen buffer
tests.why: DVS needs low latency for tight scratching.
steps: Loop output 1/2 to input 1/2 (LINE).
Set the control-panel latency to your working setting.
In Traktor Audio Setup read the reported latency (ms).

tests.title: DIN MIDI in/out through-port
tests.why: The MIDI DIN ports are only shown to Windows through the driver; a dead port breaks external gear sync.
steps: Connect a MIDI cable from DIN OUT to DIN IN (loop), or an external controller/keyboard to DIN IN.
Send notes from the controller or from a MIDI tool and exercise each key/control.
Check the messages are seen without unexpected data.

tests.title: Timecode format check: Traktor Scratch MK2 through phono input
tests.why: Confirms the interface preamp delivers a valid 2-channel quadrature timecode.
steps: Set input to PHONO (vinyl) or LINE (CDJ).
Play MK2 control vinyl at 33 1/3, stylus in the lead-in or plain area.
Run the check on each deck.

tests.title: Timecode format check: Traktor Scratch MK1
tests.why: Same for MK1 vinyl.
steps: Play MK1 control vinyl as above.

tests.title: DVS signal integrity (both decks)
tests.why: Detects dropouts, level imbalance, dirty needle on real vinyl or CD.
steps: Play control media on Deck A, run, repeat for Deck B.

tests.title: Traktor Pro install and crash/log scan
tests.why: Traktor crash logs often name the audio driver.
steps: Run the software check after a play session.

tests.title: Jacks and switches inspection
tests.why: Worn RCAs and switch contacts cause crackle.
steps: Wiggle each RCA plug in its socket while audio plays: no crackle.
Toggle each PHONO/LINE switch and confirm it clicks to both positions.
Check the headphone jack and the ground terminal tighten correctly.
Check the case for cracks and USB socket for play.

tests.title: Headphone output
tests.why: Confirms the headphone amp and any monitor routing.
steps: Connect headphones to the front headphone jack.
Play music; check both channels, clean level control, no hiss.
